title: The Program Redesign the IMF Needs
gist: Guzman and Stiglitz flag that the IMF is running its Review of Program Design and Conditionality — its first major evaluation since 2019, before COVID — and argue three features of Fund lending need reform amid widespread debt distress in developing countries.

insights.claim: The IMF is conducting a Review of Program Design and Conditionality, its first major evaluation since 2019 and therefore the first since before the COVID-19 pandemic.
insights.speaker: Martín Guzmán
insights.so_what: A live policy process that can reset terms for sovereign programs; EM debt holders should track the review's output for changes in restructuring and conditionality norms.
insights.quote: The International Monetary Fund is conducting a Review of Program Design and Conditionality, its first major evaluation since 2019, before the COVID-19 pandemic.
insights.locator: NEW YORK—The International Monetary Fund is conducting a Review

insights.claim: Widespread macroeconomic imbalances and debt distress across developing countries are severely weakening their development prospects, making IMF program-design guidelines more salient than at any prior point.
insights.speaker: Martín Guzmán
insights.so_what: Confirms a broad EM sovereign distress cycle rather than isolated cases — relevant to frontier debt spreads and restructuring supply.
insights.quote: With so many countries suffering from macroeconomic imbalances and debt distress that are severely weakening their development prospects
insights.locator: With so many countries suffering from macroeconomic imbalances

insights.claim: Three specific features of IMF lending need reform, according to the authors, who direct the review toward program design rather than the Fund's overall mandate.
insights.speaker: Martín Guzmán
insights.so_what: Narrow, targeted reform demands are more likely to land than mandate-level critiques; watch whether the review adopts them.
insights.quote: it should focus on three features of its lending, all of which need to be reformed
insights.locator: The International Monetary Fund’s guidelines for program design are more salient than ever
